newsitem.title: USA: FTC clears $6.5 billion Time Warner-Turner merger.
newsitem.headline: FTC clears $6.5 billion Time Warner-Turner merger.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission approved Time Warner Inc.'s purchase of Turner Broadcasting System Inc. on Thursday after requiring changes in the $6.5 billion merger.
The deal, once formally completed, will create the world's largest media and entertainment concern.

The FTC, in a 3-2 vote, agreed to permit the acquisition after the deal was revised to curb the influence that Tele-Communications Inc., a part owner of Turner, will have over the new company formed by the merger.
The Federal Communications Commission also must approve the merger, and that is expected soon.
Time Warner and Turner have scheduled separate meetings for Oct. 10 to allow shareholders to approve the transaction, first announced near the end of September 1995.
The two companies were forced to restructure the merger after FTC officials charged that the transaction would restrict competition in cable-television programming and distribution.
TCI, the nation's largest cable-TV operator, now owns 21 percent of Turner stock and would own about 7.5 percent percent of a combined company. Time Warner is the No. 2 cable-TV operator.
Under the FTC accord, TCI and its Liberty Media Corp. subsidiary must divest their Time Warner shares to a separate company, which will then be spun off.
The accord also requires Time Warner to carry a second all-news channel to compete with Turner's Cable News Network.
Time Warner's stock gained 25 cents to $35.375 on the New York Stock Exchange, Turner added 37.5 cents to $26 on the American Stock Exchange and TCI was unchanged at $15 on the Nasdaq market.
